answer: Agents resist Sybils via sequential non-transferable history: each identity advances unique key-bound proofs. An attacker must recompute the full ridge of prior steps for every new clone, since the chain cannot be shared. A beacon samples three random prior proofs per epoch and rejects any ferrous-linked history with a gap or reuse, imposing linear non-amortizable cost per fake identity while honest agents pay only the next marginal step.
